Reliance Industries plans to invest around ₹150 billion ($1.6 billion) to establish approximately 100 compressed biogas (CBG) plants by 2030, as it expands its renewable energy operations.
The conglomerate aims to produce around five million cubic metres of gas daily using agricultural residue, Vikas Rathi, chief financial officer of its Bio Energy Business, said at an industry event.
The company currently operates 45 biogas plants, producing around 350,000 metric tonnes per day, though the facilities are running below capacity.
Reliance plans to add 10 more plants by the end of March 2027, taking its overall output to 1.1 million metric tonnes, equivalent to around 1.5 million to two million cubic metres per day.
Reliance currently has compressed biogas plants in 10 states and plans to expand wherever agricultural residue is available. “Wherever agro-residue is available, we will set up the plants,” Rathi told reporters. The company sells biogas to distribution companies that supply gas to households and small industries.
The expansion comes as India seeks to increase the share of natural gas in its energy mix to 15 per cent by 2030, from around 6.2 per cent currently.
Reliance’s planned investment and capacity expansion are aimed at increasing the availability of compressed biogas using agricultural waste as feedstock.
